The finite lifetime τ of a level gives it an energy width (uncertainty)

 ΔE ≈ ħ / τ  (ignoring factors of 2; we only need an order–of–magnitude)

ħ = 6.6 × 10⁻¹⁶ eV·s.

For the two levels

• τ₁ = 10⁻⁹ s ⇒ ΔE₁ ≈ (6.6 × 10⁻¹⁶)/(10⁻⁹) ≈ 6.6 × 10⁻⁷ eV  
• τ₂ = 10⁻⁸ s ⇒ ΔE₂ ≈ (6.6 × 10⁻¹⁶)/(10⁻⁸) ≈ 6.6 × 10⁻⁸ eV

To “clearly resolve’’ the two lines, their separation must exceed the combined width, i.e. of order

ΔE_required ≳ ΔE₁ + ΔE₂ ≈ 7 × 10⁻⁷ eV.

Now compare with the options:

(A) 10⁻⁸ eV  < 7 × 10⁻⁷ eV  (not enough)  
(B) 10⁻⁴ eV  ≫ 7 × 10⁻⁷ eV  (safely resolvable)  
(C) 10⁻¹¹ eV  ≪ 7 × 10⁻⁷ eV  (not enough)  
(D) 10⁻⁹ eV  ≪ 7 × 10⁻⁷ eV  (not enough)

Only 10⁻⁴ eV is comfortably larger than the natural widths, so that the two levels can be distinguished without overlap.

Answer: B
